- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to recent history.
- Underestimate during sharp upward spikes; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of the spike magnitude to capture momentum.
- Overshoot in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction to recent volatility.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged bias: if true outcome is >10% above forecast at day 10+, reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day to align with observed lagged behavior.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5 days are >85% of 30-day average, cap forecast at 85% of that average for next 3 days.
